definition: The medial lemniscus is part of the dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway, an ascending route that carries somatosensory signals from the spinal cord to the ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus. In this context, it is a relay in touch-related sensory processing.

reasons: The packet mentions the dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway and the VPL receiving somatosensory inputs, but it does not directly support the specific claim that the medial lemniscus itself is the ascending relay carrying signals from the spinal cord to the ventral posterolateral nucleus.
The field label "learning" is not defensible from the packet, which is a neuroscience/neuroanatomy article about tactile reward and thalamic inactivation rather than learning.

The packet only states that the VPL “receives somatosensory inputs from the spinal cord via the dorsal column–medial lemniscus pathway”; it does not define “medial lemniscus” itself as a specific anatomical part or component.

Claims that it is “an ascending route” and “carries somatosensory signals from the spinal cord to the ventral posterolateral nucleus of the thalamus” are not explicitly supported as the definition’s referent; the packet supports the pathway-to-VPL idea, not the independent definition of the medial lemniscus component.

The statement that it is “a relay in touch-related sensory processing” is not directly supported by the packet (it provides no explicit “relay” role wording or touch-processing description tied specifically to the medial lemniscus).
